note: GPU milliseconds at 2560x1440, measured in the live game loop by tools/gate-perf.mjs. 'aspiration' is the PERFORMANCE.md contract (60 fps on the M5 Pro at full window, 30+ on an integrated-GPU Windows laptop at 1080p). 'ceiling' is the regression guard: the gate fails above it. MEASURE AGAINST THE DEPLOYED URL when it matters — a local run on this machine reads up to 2x slow when anything else is building (M35: live 3.3-5.3 ms vs local 6-9.5 ms, same commit). The ceilings below are set ~60% above the clean live numbers so ordinary contention does not flake the gate; tighten them with --write after a lever wins, and never loosen one without a line in CHECKLIST.md. M42/M43: the ceilings now include the DEFAULT POST STACK (grade + FXAA + atmosphere + bloom, about 1.1 ms — see tools/qa-post.mjs for the layer price list). They were raised from 11/9/8 for that reason and no other. M58: `wallP50` is a CPU ceiling, in wall-clock milliseconds at the p50 of the same runs. It exists because M58's prototype sharing cut the CPU frame from 7.9 to 4.7-4.9 ms with the GPU unchanged, and nothing in this gate would have noticed that being given back. M64 raised it 9 → 14: 9 was NOT generous enough. The same note two lines up says a local run reads up to 2x slow when anything else is building, and 4.7 x 2 is 9.4 — the ceiling flaked at a load average of 12, reading 9.2 ms. 14 still catches a tripling; a real regression is never 20%.
